title: "Swiss municipalities"
description: "Official services for municipality states, correspondences and mutations."

<div class="toolbox-kind">Resource · verified 2026-10-04</div>

## Services

| Need | Endpoint | Verified output |
|---|---|---|
| Geographic levels at a date | `https://sms.bfs.admin.ch/WcfBFSSpecificService.svc/AnonymousRest/communes/levels` | CSV with municipality, OFS code and geographic-level code/label pairs |
| Correspondence between dates | `https://sms.bfs.admin.ch/WcfBFSSpecificService.svc/AnonymousRest/communes/correspondances` | CSV with initial and terminal historical/OFS codes, names, parents and steps |
| Municipality mutations | `https://www.agvchapp.bfs.admin.ch/api/communes/mutations` | CSV with mutation number/date and initial/terminal municipality fields |

The services accept dates formatted as `DD-MM-YYYY`. Read mapping columns as character data: several geographic classifications contain meaningful leading zeroes.

## Shared response reader

The three helpers retain the established URLs and parameters. The shared reader adds status checking, optional raw-response preservation and character-safe parsing.

```r
library(tidyverse)
library(httr2)
library(janitor)
library(here)

raw_dir <- here("input", "raw")

read_bfs_csv <- function(url, raw_path = NULL) {
  response <- request(url) |>
    req_headers(Accept = "text/csv") |>
    req_perform()
  resp_check_status(response)

  temporary <- is.null(raw_path)
  path <- if (temporary) tempfile(fileext = ".csv") else raw_path
  if (!temporary) dir.create(dirname(path), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

  writeBin(resp_body_raw(response), path)
  result <- read_csv(
    path,
    col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
    na = c("", "NA")
  )

  if (temporary) unlink(path)
  result
}
```

## Geographic levels at a date

```r
get_geolevel <- function(date1, raw_path = NULL) {
  url <- str_c(
    "https://sms.bfs.admin.ch/WcfBFSSpecificService.svc/AnonymousRest/communes/levels?",
    "startPeriod=", date1,
    "&endPeriod=", date1,
    "&useBfsCode=false",
    "&labelLanguages=fr",
    "&format=csv"
  )

  read_bfs_csv(url, raw_path)
}

spatial_index <- get_geolevel(
  "18-10-2020",
  file.path(raw_dir, "bfs_geolevel_2020-10-18.csv")
) |>
  clean_names()

spatial_index |>
  select(identifier, name_fr, code_ofs, starts_with("hr_")) |>
  glimpse()
```

The response pairs classification codes with translated labels, for example `hr_regch` and `hr_regch_name_fr`. Select only the classifications needed for the analysis rather than carrying the very wide table everywhere.

## Correspondence between two dates

```r
get_geocoding_bfs <- function(date1, date2, raw_path = NULL) {
  url <- str_c(
    "https://sms.bfs.admin.ch/WcfBFSSpecificService.svc/AnonymousRest/communes/correspondances?",
    "includeUnmodified=true",
    "&includeTerritoryExchange=false",
    "&startPeriod=", date1,
    "&endPeriod=", date2
  )

  read_bfs_csv(url, raw_path)
}

bfs_key_raw <- get_geocoding_bfs(
  "01-01-2020",
  "01-06-2023",
  file.path(raw_dir, "bfs_correspondence_2020-01-01_2023-06-01.csv")
) |>
  clean_names()

bfs_key_raw |>
  select(initial_code, initial_name, terminal_code, terminal_name) |>
  glimpse()
```

`includeUnmodified=true` keeps municipalities whose OFS code did not change, which makes this response suitable as a complete join key for a known source state. Territory exchanges are excluded here because they do not represent a whole-municipality mapping.

## Municipality mutations

```r
get_communes_mutations_bfs <- function(date1, date2, raw_path = NULL) {
  url <- str_c(
    "https://www.agvchapp.bfs.admin.ch/api/communes/mutations?",
    "includeTerritoryExchange=false",
    "&Deleted=True",
    "&Created=True",
    "&startPeriod=", date1,
    "&endPeriod=", date2
  )

  read_bfs_csv(url, raw_path)
}

bfs_communes_mutations <- get_communes_mutations_bfs(
  "01-01-2008",
  "02-01-2013",
  file.path(raw_dir, "bfs_commune_mutations_2008-01-01_2013-01-02.csv")
) |>
  clean_names() |>
  mutate(mutation_date = lubridate::dmy(mutation_date))
```

A simple inspection key can reproduce an existing workflow:

```r
mutation_key <- bfs_communes_mutations |>
  arrange(mutation_date) |>
  group_by(initial_code) |>
  summarise(final_code = last(terminal_code), .groups = "drop")
```

This is not automatically a harmonization key. It does not resolve transitive chains such as `A → B → C`, and it cannot allocate a true split. Prefer the correspondence endpoint for a known source and target date; use mutations to understand and audit exceptional histories.

See [Harmonize historical municipalities](../recipes/municipality-harmonization.qmd).
